evidence.mechanism: shot-08s: six arms with perpendicular side ticks grow from a centre cluster of overlapping t/c/e/f glyphs; the fixed-lag row of letters behind a tip is not legible. By shot-20s the arms gain more ticks.
evidence.ambition: shot-02s: one flat vector star on a radial rose gradient with dashed centre lines; by shot-20s side ticks and glyph layers add to it, but there is no material, lighting or simulation pass.
evidence.craft: shot-02s: clean oxblood on clay palette, but the arm roots are cut square and the dashed centre rules look broken. By shot-20s the glyph pile at the centre overlaps into clutter.
evidence.distinctness: shot-02s: rose-clay and oxblood six-arm dendrite, unlike the cream and ochre Penrose tiling of 2026-11-23; the six-armed snowflake silhouette is itself a familiar demoscene form.
evidence.polish: shot-02s: figure is centred and fills much of the frame at start; by shot-20s the full six-fold figure is whole, with ticks densest and glyph clutter at the centre unresolved.

pairwise_justification: Median Penrose 8s shows a dense ochre-and-rust tiling on cream with clean edges; tonight's 8s is a dark star with overlapping t/c/e/f glyphs piled at the centre, so the median wins the head-to-head.

critique.change: At shot-08s, spread the glyphs of defect into one row at a constant spacing just behind the tip, each swelling into its own arm, instead of piling them at the centre; drop the V/R readout.
Taper each arm root into the centre instead of the square-cut notches visible at shot-02s, and make the dashed centre rule continuous so it does not break into dashes.
Give the arms one shaded ridge or light falloff so the figure has a second rendering layer beyond flat fills; by shot-20s let early arms stop short so arm length visibly differs.
